title: Outbound messages, webhooks, polling, retries, idempotency, and dead-letter handling

objectives: Place outbound messages, webhooks, and polling on the INT-003 style map (fire-and-forget vs request/response vs scheduled pull).
Design retries with backoff and a dead-letter path after poison messages.
Require idempotency keys so at-least-once delivery does not double-apply.
Prefer named-credential REST or events over new SOAP outbound-message designs unless the endpoint already demands OM.
diagnostic_question: A SOAP listener missed a message, a webhook was delivered twice, and a poller hammered Limits. What do retries, idempotency, and dead-letter handling each do—and when is outbound messaging the wrong push?
definition: Fire-and-forget integrations still fail. Salesforce outbound messaging delivers a SOAP notification to an endpoint with platform retries. Webhooks are HTTP callbacks (often implemented with named-credential callouts or middleware). Polling pulls on a schedule. Retries repeat failed deliveries; idempotency makes duplicates safe; a dead-letter path isolates poison messages. ([Integration Patterns Fire and Forget](https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/fundamentals/guide/integration-patterns); [Apex named callouts](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_callouts_named_credentials.htm))
why_it_matters: At-least-once delivery without idempotency double-charges. Infinite retries without a dead letter melt APIs (INT-005). Interviewers want the trio: retry, idempotent, dead-letter.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of certified mail. Outbound messaging is a postal SOAP truck with built-in retries. A webhook is a courier knocking on an HTTP door. Polling is you visiting the post office on a schedule. Retries send the truck again. Idempotency is a tracking number so two trucks do not cash the same check. The dead-letter office holds parcels that fail until a human opens them—not an infinite retry loop.
deeper_explanation: Official Fire and Forget: Salesforce does not wait for remote completion. Outbound messaging is a classic declarative SOAP implementation of that style. New work often uses platform events (INT-007) or named-credential HTTP (INT-006). Workflow-rule retirement dates are org-policy—Needs verification; prefer Flow-triggered OM if OM is required.

Retries: transient 5xx/timeout vs permanent 4xx. Tight loops on 403 REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (INT-005) are harmful. Exponential backoff is a practice; exact Salesforce OM retry schedule is in Help—do not invent hours here.

Idempotency: process the same delivery key once. Store Salesforce Id plus a change stamp or event id (INT-007). At-least-once is the usual contract; exactly-once is a myth unless you build idempotency.
Dead-letter: after N failures, stop automated retry, alert, keep payload for replay. Without it, poison JSON (INT-005 400) retries forever.

mental_model.analogy: Certified mail: SOAP truck (outbound message), HTTP knock (webhook), visiting the desk (polling), extra trucks (retries), tracking numbers (idempotency), dead-letter office (poison parcels).
useful_mapping: outbound message → SOAP certified truck from Salesforce
polling → scheduled visit to their desk
retry → send the truck again for transient faults
dead letter → held parcel + alert, not infinite trucks
named credential callout → prepaid envelope from INT-006
platform event → radio DVR from INT-007
where_it_breaks: OM retry schedule is documented in Help, not this analogy's 'three days'.
Webhooks are not a Salesforce product name; they are an HTTP pattern.
Polling burns API limits if naive.
Dead-letter is a design, not a Setup checkbox unless a product provides one.

claims.claim: Fire and Forget does not wait for remote completion; outbound messaging is a SOAP notification style used for that pattern. HTTP callouts with named credentials are the usual JSON webhook-style implementation from Apex.
claims.validation: Patterns plus callout plus OM Help.

claims.claim: Event replay can redeliver; subscribers must treat delivery as at-least-once and apply idempotency (store Replay ID / event id).
HTTP 403 REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED must not be tight-retried (INT-005). Poison 400 bodies need a dead-letter path rather than infinite retry.
claims.validation: Combined with REST error-codes lesson; patterns require error handling.

claims.claim: Polling is a client-initiated pull; it consumes API request allocations when pointed at Salesforce APIs.
claims.validation: Remote Call-In / API limits context in patterns document.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: OM is SOAP push with platform retries. Webhooks are HTTP pushes you build. Polling pulls. Retries handle transients. Idempotency makes duplicates safe. Dead letters stop poison loops.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I assume at-least-once. I pick a key (record Id + version or event id). Transient 503 backs off; 400 goes to dead letter; 403 limits do not hot-loop. New designs prefer events or named-credential HTTP unless the partner is already an OM SOAP listener. Workflow OM availability Needs verification; I would use Flow if OM is required.

terminology.plain: Salesforce SOAP-notifies a URL you registered.
terminology.precise: Declarative outbound messaging sends SOAP to an endpoint; platform retries. Confirm current Help for session, fields, and retry timing.
terminology.example: Legacy ERP SOAP listener receiving Opportunity notifications.
terminology.boundary: Triggering automation (Flow vs workflow) Needs verification.

terminology.precise: Not a single Salesforce product name. Usually Apex/middleware HTTP POST using named credentials (INT-006) or a partner's inbound URL.
terminology.example: POST JSON to a billing endpoint on Closed Won.
terminology.boundary: Signature verification is vendor-specific—do not invent HMAC details.

terminology.plain: You ask on a schedule instead of being pushed.
terminology.precise: Client-initiated pull (REST Query, Bulk, or remote GET). Burns limits if naive (INT-005).
terminology.example: Every 15 minutes GET remote status when they cannot push.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Scheduled Apex as the timer, not the pattern name.

terminology.plain: Send again after a transient failure.
terminology.precise: Re-attempt delivery with backoff. Distinguish 5xx/timeout from 4xx poison and 403 limits.
terminology.example: Retry 503 three times with backoff, then dead-letter.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Event replay (INT-007) which is resume, not HTTP retry.
terminology.boundary: OM retry table: Help, not invented hours.

terminology.plain: Two trucks with the same tracking number cash the check once.
terminology.precise: Processing the same business key twice yields one effect. Store keys (Id, event id, Replay ID + event id).
terminology.example: Upsert by External Id; ignore second Closed Won webhook with same Opportunity Id and LastModifiedDate.
terminology.non_example: Insert a payment row on every HTTP retry.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Salesforce Id uniqueness ≠ your side effects are unique.
terminology.boundary: Exactly-once delivery is not promised by the bus.

terminology.plain: Hold poison parcels for humans, stop the infinite truck.
terminology.precise: After N failures or on non-retryable errors, persist payload, alert, halt auto-retry.
terminology.example: 400 malformed JSON from INT-005 goes to LAB_DeadLetter__c plus email.
terminology.boundary: No single Setup checkbox unless a product provides a DLQ.

terminology.plain: You might see the same mail twice; design for that.
terminology.precise: Common contract for OM retries, HTTP retries, and event replay. Requires idempotency.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Request/response 201 that the user waited for (still can double-click).

terminology.plain: A parcel that will never succeed as-is.
terminology.precise: Typically permanent 4xx / schema errors. Dead-letter, do not backoff-retry forever.

when_to_use: When designing outbound messages, webhooks, polling, retries, idempotency, and dead-letter handling together.
When a partner already exposes a SOAP outbound-message listener and OM is the agreed push.
When HTTP webhooks or polling would otherwise double-apply or hot-loop limits.
When event replay (INT-007) makes duplicate processing likely.
When poison 400 responses must stop automated retries.
when_not_to_use: Do not invent OM retry hours; read Help.
Do not use OM SOAP as the default for a new JSON API (prefer named-credential callout or events).
Do not poll Salesforce REST every second (INT-005 limits).
Do not skip idempotency because 'SOAP is reliable'.
Do not build production DLQs with real payments in this lesson.

interview_questions.question: Cover outbound messages, webhooks, polling, retries, idempotency, and dead-letter handling.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: OM SOAP push with retries. Webhooks HTTP push. Polling pull. Retry transients. Idempotency for duplicates. Dead letter for poison.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I assume at-least-once delivery. Outbound messages are SOAP push with platform retries; webhooks are HTTP push; polling is a pull. I add idempotency keys and a dead-letter path. I will not invent outbound-message retry hours; I open Help. Platform events still need this trio.
interview_questions.example: Closed Won JSON webhook with a duplicate POST and a 400.

interview_questions.question: Why is exactly-once the wrong promise?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Retries and replay exist. Promise idempotent at-least-once instead.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Pub/Sub durability notes and HTTP retries can deliver the same payload twice. Exactly-once is the wrong promise. I put a unique business key in front of money side effects and treat the integration as idempotent at-least-once, including outbound messages and webhooks.
interview_questions.example: Invoice External Id equals Opportunity Id so a duplicate POST cannot bill twice.

interview_questions.question: ERP has only a SOAP OM listener this year.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Use outbound messaging, confirm Help retry/session notes, still design idempotency on their side.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I will not force GraphQL. I check how OM is invoked after workflow changes—Needs verification. Long-term I might bridge to events.
interview_questions.example: Existing ERP WSDL listener can accept only SOAP outbound messages this fiscal year.

interview_questions.question: Startups want a webhook; they double-POST.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Named-credential callout plus idempotency store; 4xx to DLQ.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I send the webhook through a named-credential callout (INT-006), branch on HTTP status (INT-005), and store an idempotency key so a double POST cannot create two invoices. Poison 400 goes to a dead-letter queue; I do not tight-loop 403 REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Invoice__c unique External Id test that replays the same webhook POST twice.

interview_questions.question: An outbound message never arrives at the ERP SOAP listener. How do you diagnose it?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Endpoint reachability, automation entry, OM delivery status in Help—not Replay ID.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I distinguish SOAP outbound messaging from Pub/Sub replay. I check endpoint reachability, the automation that fires the message, firewall and certificates, and Help delivery status. I do not invent retry hours and I do not treat a missing OM as a Replay ID problem.
interview_questions.example: Sandbox OM to a listener that only allowed production IPs.

interview_questions.question: Poller hits 403 limits.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Slow the poll, use CDC/Pub/Sub if they can subscribe, or Bulk for extracts.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I slow the poll and read Limits Remaining (INT-005). If the partner can subscribe, I switch to CDC or platform events on Pub/Sub (INT-007). For large extracts I consider Bulk 2.0. Polling every few seconds is an anti-pattern against REST rate limits.
interview_questions.example: A 30-second Account SOQL poller that burns Daily API Requests until HTTP 403.

interview_questions.question: How many retries before dead letter?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I pick a finite N for transients and I do not quote a fake OM table. Poison 400 goes immediately to DLQ.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I pick a finite N for transient failures in the runbook and I Needs-verify outbound-message built-in retries so we do not double-retry blindly. A poison 400 goes immediately to the dead-letter queue with an alert; I will not quote a fake Help table of hours.
interview_questions.example: N equals 5 exponential backoff for HTTP 503; HTTP 400 goes immediately to DLQ.

interview_questions.question: Teach certified-mail analogy and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Trucks, knocks, desk visits, extra trucks, tracking numbers, dead-letter office. It breaks when I invent OM hours or call webhook a product.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Certified mail maps outbound messages to trucks, webhooks to knocks, polling to desk visits, retries to extra trucks, idempotency to tracking numbers, and dead letters to the undeliverable office. It breaks when I invent OM retry hours or treat webhook as a Salesforce product name. Events belong on the radio bus in INT-007, not on this mail route.
